title: Round-trip of the restriction encoder and decoder
statement: Let $f$ be a DNF formula on $n$ variables whose width is at most $w$, and suppose that within every term of $f$ any two literals naming the same variable are in fact equal. Given a natural number serving as a step budget for the encoder, a finite list of variable–value pairs, and a restriction $\rho$ on the $n$ variables, encoding $\rho$ relative to $f$ produces a list from which the decoder — run with a step budget one larger than that list's length — recovers $\rho$ exactly.
hypotheses_covered: f is a DNF formula on n variables
the width of f is at most w
within each term, literals sharing a variable are equal
a natural-number step budget for the encoder (enc_fuel)
a finite list of variable-value pairs (path)
a restriction rho on the n variables

The hypotheses (width bound, per-term variable distinctness, encoder step budget, list of variable-value pairs, and restriction) are recoverable, but the precise conclusion — the exact roles of the step budget and the pair list, and the exact sense of the round-trip — is inferred only from the untrusted `current` hint and cannot be verified against the ground truth.
